questions.note: Height, head top, shoulder line, carrier bottom and foot positions register well in the onion. But the upper arms and forearms read as thick uniform tubes, the shoulders sit wider and squarer than the drawn sloping shoulders, and the head reads broad. Leg lengths differ only as declared.

The stance, the foot spread and the carbine's diagonal overlay the reference closely. The head faces the camera instead of the drawn three-quarter turn to his left with the chin raised. His right elbow flares about 35 px wider, and the shoulder silhouette is boxy where the drawn pauldrons are rounded.

Every item is present and roughly placed. But the pauldrons are flat brown boards, not curved steel-grey shells. The left forearm guard sits at the elbow, not over the forearm to the wrist. The right forearm guard is a stack of rings. The right thigh rig is two kydex mag holders where the drawing has a holster platform. The right knee pad sits off to the side, and the carrier front is stripped.

Most layers sit on what is under them. But the right knee pad stands off the outer knee. A rear belt pouch hinges out into the air behind the hip. The back panel rides high and leaves a band of shirt bare above the belt. Two rods dangle under the thigh pouches, and leg-strap slider hardware floats on the trouser surface.

The reference has a loose combat shirt and trousers under bulky kit. The render's shirt and seat read skin-tight, like a compression suit, with the crotch and buttocks modelled through the trousers. The carrier is a thin flat slab with three short pouches where the drawing has a deep, laden plate carrier. The pauldrons and guards are thin, flat plates.

The carbine's line matches the drawn diagonal. His right hand is on the pistol grip with the index finger straight along the receiver, and his left hand wraps the handguard, so the hold is real. But the gloved fingers are long and smooth, and the right hand's curled fingers barely close. The left hand sits a little higher on the handguard than drawn.

defects.what: His right knee pad hangs off the outer side of the knee as a flat shell standing off the leg, instead of being centred over the kneecap and strapped to it; in the onion it sits about 80 px toward the viewer's left of the drawn pad.
defects.fix: Centre the cap on the patella and wrap it around the front of the knee, with straps behind the knee holding it against the trouser, as on the left leg.

defects.what: A pouch at the back of the belt hinges open and tilts away from the belt into the air; the same object shows behind the hip in side_R and back views, floating off the body.
defects.fix: Mount it flat against the belt's outer face, held by its belt loops or MOLLE straps.

defects.what: The pauldrons are flat, angular, dark-brown boards with tan speckle. The reference has curved, cool steel-grey hard shells that cap the shoulder in two overlapping segments. His right one is the same flat flap.
defects.fix: Domed shoulder caps with a second curved segment below, painted blue-grey with worn edges, as in the reference.

defects.what: The emblem on the left pauldron is a pointed tab with a V or crown chevron; the reference has a rounded-square plate bearing a crossed X mark.
defects.fix: Match the drawn emblem's shape and mark: a rounded-square plate with the crossed X.

defects.what: The carrier front is a plain flat plate with three short pouches, in dark brown. The reference has an olive-coyote carrier with an admin panel, wide padded shoulder straps with buckles and four or more tall flapped mag pouches.
defects.fix: Add the admin or placard panel, the tall flapped triple or quad mag pouches and the padded straps, and shift the colour toward worn olive coyote.

defects.what: The left forearm guard is a ribbed tube sitting over the elbow and upper forearm, leaving bare sleeve down to the glove; the reference has a separate elbow pad plus a plated guard running from mid forearm to the wrist.
defects.fix: Add an elbow pad on the point of the elbow and move the plated guard down so it ends at the glove cuff.

defects.what: His right forearm guard is a stack of plain cylindrical rings; the reference shows a long, shaped gauntlet plate with straps and layered panels covering the forearm.
defects.fix: Build a contoured forearm plate with edge rims and strap hardware that follows the forearm's taper.

defects.what: The right boot's vamp is a smooth, sock-like wedge with no toe cap, no eyelets and no lacing below the ankle, like a slip-on sneaker. The reference boot is laced to the toe, with a scuffed rand and a toe bumper.
defects.fix: Carry the eyelets and lacing down the vamp and add the toe cap, rand and mudguard panels as on the left boot.

defects.what: The head faces the camera almost square on. The reference turns the head about 30 degrees to his left (viewer's right) and lifts the chin so that he looks up and off-frame.
defects.fix: Rotate the head and neck to the drawn yaw and pitch.

defects.what: The hair is a smooth, uniform cap with a hard straight hairline, like a helmet. The reference has a short textured crop, longer and swept up on top, with faded sides and an irregular hairline.
defects.fix: Give the top volume and spiky texture, fade the sides, and break up the hairline.

defects.what: The trousers and shirt fit like a compression suit: the crotch is a smooth anatomical bulge and the seat in the back view is modelled skin-tight. The reference trousers are loose ripstop with volume through the hips and thighs.
defects.fix: Give the trousers combat-cut ease: drape at the fly, and fabric that bridges the crotch and the seat rather than following the body.

defects.what: His right thigh carries two flat, rigid, kydex-like mag holders. The reference has a drop-leg platform with a holster-type body and a pouch, on two wide leg straps with buckles.
defects.fix: Build a drop-leg platform with a holster shell and a flapped pouch, slung from the belt and held by two buckled thigh straps.

defects.what: Two thin rods with knobs dangle below the thigh pouches; the reference has nothing like them.
defects.fix: Remove them, or make them limp pull tabs or bungee ends lying against the pouch.

defects.what: Leg-strap slider hardware shows as floating rectangular slots printed on the trouser surface, with no strap continuing through them.
defects.fix: Thread the strap through its slider so that both lie on the trouser together.

defects.what: The gloves are smooth, featureless rubber with long tapering fingers; the reference gloves are M-Pact-type with knuckle armour, padded finger segments and a visible cuff.
defects.fix: Add the moulded knuckle guard, finger pads and cuff tab, and shorten the fingers to his hand's proportions.

defects.what: The back panel is small and rides high, leaving a band of bare shirt between the carrier and the belt all the way round the lower back.
defects.fix: Size the back plate and cummerbund like a real JPC-class carrier so that the bottom edge sits at the drawn front height, just above the belt.

defects.what: The upper arms and forearms are thick, uniform cylinders, and his right elbow flares wider than drawn, so the arms read heavier and stiffer than the reference's fitted sleeves.
defects.fix: Taper the sleeves to the arm, with folds at the elbow, and bring the elbow in to the drawn silhouette.

defects.what: The knee pads are tall, flat rectangles with a tan rim band. The reference pads are faceted, articulated hard caps with a hexagonal central plate and tan-edged rims, shorter and domed.
defects.fix: Shape the cap as a domed, faceted shell with the drawn central plate and rim.

defects.what: The muzzle device is bright, polished copper; the reference muzzle is dark, parkerized steel like the rest of the gun.
defects.fix: Make it a dark phosphate or black-oxide finish with worn edges.

defects.what: There is a small optic on top at the front of the receiver, and no weapon light on the side of the handguard, where the reference shows a cylindrical light mounted at the rail beside his left forearm.
defects.fix: Mount a weapon light on the handguard's side rail where drawn.

defects.what: The left hip pouch is a single wide dark-brown box with a snap next to a black block; the reference has a tall olive double mag pouch with flaps.
defects.fix: Make it a flapped double pouch in worn olive coyote.

ranked: [D5] The carrier is the biggest give-away: a thin, flat brown slab with three stubby pouches, where the reference has a laden olive-coyote plate carrier with an admin panel, padded straps and four or more tall flapped mag pouches.
[D3] The pauldrons are flat brown boards bolted on at angles. The reference's curved steel-grey shoulder shells are a signature of this man's kit and change the whole shoulder silhouette.

[D11] The clothing fits like a wetsuit. The crotch and seat are sculpted through the trousers and the shirt clings to the torso, so he reads as a mannequin in leggings, not a soldier in loose ripstop.
[D17] The arms are heavy, uniform tubes with his right elbow flared out; the reference's sleeves taper and fold, and its elbows sit closer in.
[D9] The head faces the camera. The reference's three-quarter turn to his left with the chin lifted is a large part of the pose's character and of the likeness.

[D10] The hair is a smooth helmet with a hard hairline, not the reference's textured, swept-up crop with faded sides. Together with the declared parametric face and default skin, he does not read as the same man.
[D1] His right knee pad stands off the outer knee instead of capping the kneecap; it reads as a loose flap.
[D2] A rear belt pouch hinges out into the air behind the hip, visible in every side and back view.
[D16] Seen from behind, the carrier is a small high panel with bare shirt showing all round between it and the belt; a real carrier and cummerbund would reach down to the belt.

[D6] On the left arm the guard sits over the elbow, the elbow pad is missing and the forearm is bare down to the glove. The reference has an elbow pad plus a plated forearm guard that runs to the wrist.
[D7] His right forearm guard is a stack of plain rings rather than the reference's long, shaped gauntlet.
[D12] His right thigh rig has the wrong identity: two flat kydex mag holders where the reference has a drop-leg holster platform on two buckled leg straps.
[D8] The right boot's vamp is a smooth, laceless wedge, like a slip-on sneaker; the left boot is laced, so the pair don't even match each other.
[D15] The gloves are smooth rubber with long tapering fingers; the reference's knuckle-armoured tactical gloves are blockier and more padded.
[D18] The knee pads are tall flat rectangles; the reference's are domed, faceted caps with a central plate.
[D4] The pauldron emblem is the wrong mark and shape: a pointed V or crown tab instead of the rounded-square plate with a crossed X.

The colour palette is shifted. The carrier and pouches are dark chocolate brown instead of worn olive coyote, and the pauldrons are brown instead of blue-grey steel. The shirt reads brown-grey rather than the reference's near-black, even allowing for the warm, ungraded key.
The wear is uniform tan speckle stamped on every hard plate. The reference's wear is edge-driven scuffing and dirt that differs by material, so the render's kit reads newer and more toy-like.
[D21] The left hip pouch is a single dark box beside a black block, not the tall olive double mag pouch drawn there.
[D20] The weapon light on the handguard's side is missing, and a small optic stands on the receiver instead.
[D13] Two rods with knobs dangle below the right thigh pouches; they belong to nothing in the reference.
[D14] Leg-strap sliders float on the trouser surface with no strap through them.
[D19] The bright copper muzzle device catches the eye; the reference's gun is uniformly dark, apart from its tan accents.
The trouser legs pile into a heavy, even bunch above the boots and lack the reference's lower-leg reinforcement panels and irregular blousing.
